sinon.stub(obj, "prop").get(fn) and sinon.stub(obj, "prop").set(fn) install the replacement function directly as the property's accessor, so reading or writing the stubbed property runs the replacement untracked: nothing records the access and there is no call count to assert on. Wrap the replacement getter and the replacement setter in a spy and expose the spies on the stub as stub.getter and stub.setter, mirroring the spy.get and spy.set surface that sinon.spy(obj, "prop", ["get"]) produces. That surface is the whole sinon spy API, not a call counter: stub.getter and stub.setter must be sinon spies on which everything sinon.spy(fn) returns supports works the same way, among them callCount, calledOnce and calledThrice, calledWith, withArgs, getCall and firstCall, args, returnValues and resetHistory; a wrapper that only counts calls does not meet this. After const stub = sinon.stub(obj, "prop").get(() => "bar"), reading obj.prop three times must give "bar" each time and stub.getter.callCount must be 3 (stub.getter.calledThrice true); after const stub = sinon.stub(obj, "prop").set((value) => { obj.example = value }), assigning obj.prop = "bar" then obj.prop = "baz" must run the setter both times (obj.example is "baz") with stub.setter.callCount 2, stub.setter.calledWith("bar") true and stub.setter.withArgs("bar").callCount 1. stub.resetBehavior() must remove both, so stub.getter and stub.setter are undefined afterwards. Everything .get and .set do today must stay: the replacement runs, the property is defined configurable as before, restore works, and .get and .set stay chainable. Source is ESM under src/sinon/ (default-behaviors.js holds the get and set behaviours, stub.js the stub prototype, spy.js makes spies); the node tests run with npm run test-node (mocha over test/src, test/issues and test/scripts).
